outcome: Pulmonary function test measures (PC 20 ≤ 25 mg/mL, % predicted forced vital capacity [FVC], forced expiratory volume in 1 second [FEV(1)]/FVC, forced expiratory flow from 25% to 75% of vital capacity [FEF(25-75)])
cohort: 481 children from the WHEALS birth cohort
finding: Black children experienced worse allergic outcomes than white children by age 10 years, including higher rates of eczema, asthma, sensitization, and worse pulmonary function, and these differences could not be explained by confounding factors.
mod_finding: While the abstract reports differences in allergic outcomes between Black and white children, there were subgroup variations in the magnitude of association within delivery mode.
